description: Point-level tennis-rules MCQ bank (canonical options + stem variants).

questions.name: legal_serve_landing_location
questions.title: Legal serve landing location
questions.question: According to the rules of singles tennis, where must a legal serve land for the serve to be valid?
question_stems: According to the rules of singles tennis, where must a legal serve land for the serve to be valid?
Under singles rules, which location makes a serve legal?
Where is a serve required to land in order to be valid in singles?
For a singles serve to count as good, where must the ball land?
options: In the service box diagonally opposite the server
Anywhere inside the opponent’s singles court
In either service box on the opponent’s side of the net
On or beyond the opponent’s baseline after the bounce
questions.correct_answer: In the service box diagonally opposite the server

questions.name: first_serve_fault
questions.title: First-serve fault
questions.question: If the server commits a fault on the first serve, what is the correct continuation of the point?
question_stems: If the server commits a fault on the first serve, what is the correct continuation of the point?
After a fault on the first serve, what happens next on that point?
What is the ruling when the server faults the opening serve of a point?
The first serve is a fault. How does the point continue?
options: The server immediately loses the point
The server is awarded a second serve on the same point
The receiver may choose whether the point is replayed
The players change ends and the entire point is restarted
questions.correct_answer: The server is awarded a second serve on the same point

questions.name: double_fault
questions.title: Double fault
questions.question: If the server faults on both the first serve and the second serve, what is the official result?
question_stems: If the server faults on both the first serve and the second serve, what is the official result?
What is the result of consecutive faults on first and second serve?
When both serve attempts of a point are faults, who wins the point and why?
A first-serve fault is followed by a second-serve fault. What is the ruling?
options: The server is granted a third serve
The point is replayed from the beginning
The receiver is awarded the point (double fault)
The score remains unchanged and the server serves again on a later point
questions.correct_answer: The receiver is awarded the point (double fault)

questions.name: let_serve_that_lands_in
questions.title: Let serve that lands in
questions.question: A serve touches the net and then lands in the correct service box. What is the correct ruling?
question_stems: A serve touches the net and then lands in the correct service box. What is the correct ruling?
If a serve clips the net and still lands in the proper service box, what happens?
What is the call when a serve hits the net cord and then lands in?
A net-cord serve lands in the correct box. What is the official decision?
options: The server wins the point
The serve is counted as a fault
The receiver wins the point
The serve is a let, and that serve attempt is replayed
questions.correct_answer: The serve is a let, and that serve attempt is replayed

questions.name: serve_that_touches_the_net_and_lands_out
questions.title: Serve that touches the net and lands out
questions.question: A serve touches the net and then lands outside the correct service box. What is the correct ruling?
question_stems: A serve touches the net and then lands outside the correct service box. What is the correct ruling?
If a serve clips the net and then lands out of the service box, what is the call?
What is the ruling for a net-cord serve that fails to land in the correct box?
A serve hits the net and then misses the service box. How is it judged?
options: The serve is a fault
The serve is a let and must be replayed
The receiver automatically wins the point
The entire point is replayed regardless of the score
questions.correct_answer: The serve is a fault

questions.name: definition_of_an_ace
questions.title: Definition of an ace
questions.question: Which of the following correctly defines an ace?
question_stems: Which of the following correctly defines an ace?
What is the definition of an ace in tennis?
Which statement accurately describes an ace?
How is an ace correctly defined under tennis rules?
options: Any serve that the receiver touches but fails to return in court
A serve that lands in and is not touched by the receiver
A non-serve groundstroke that lands in and is not reached by the opponent
A second serve that lands in after a fault on the first serve
questions.correct_answer: A serve that lands in and is not touched by the receiver

questions.name: ball_landing_on_a_line
questions.title: Ball landing on a line
questions.question: During a point, a shot lands on the singles sideline. Under the rules, how is the ball judged?
question_stems: During a point, a shot lands on the singles sideline. Under the rules, how is the ball judged?
If a ball lands on the singles sideline during a point, is it in or out?
How do the rules treat a ball that touches the singles sideline?
A shot hits the singles sideline. What is the correct in/out ruling?
options: The ball is out, because the line is outside the court
The point is replayed as a let
The ball is in, because the line is part of the court
The ball is out unless confirmed otherwise by electronic line calling
questions.correct_answer: The ball is in, because the line is part of the court

questions.name: double_bounce
questions.title: Double bounce
questions.question: If the ball bounces twice on a player’s side of the court before that player returns it, who wins the point?
question_stems: If the ball bounces twice on a player’s side of the court before that player returns it, who wins the point?
Who wins the point when a player lets the ball bounce twice before returning it?
After a second bounce on one side, what is the ruling?
The ball bounces twice before being played. Who is awarded the point?
options: The player who allowed the second bounce
Neither player; the point is replayed as a let
The server, regardless of which player failed to play the ball
The opponent of the player who allowed the second bounce
questions.correct_answer: The opponent of the player who allowed the second bounce

questions.name: touching_the_net_while_the_ball_is_in_play
questions.title: Touching the net while the ball is in play
questions.question: While the ball is in play, a player touches the net with the racket or body. What is the correct ruling?
question_stems: While the ball is in play, a player touches the net with the racket or body. What is the correct ruling?
What happens if a player touches the net during a live point?
A player makes contact with the net while the ball is in play. What is the call?
Under the rules, what is the result of touching the net during a point?
options: The player who touched the net loses the point
Play continues unless the ball also touches the net
The point is automatically replayed as a let
The player receives a warning and the point is restarted
questions.correct_answer: The player who touched the net loses the point

questions.name: ball_striking_a_player
questions.title: Ball striking a player
questions.question: During a rally, a legal shot strikes the opponent’s body before bouncing. What is the correct result?
question_stems: During a rally, a legal shot strikes the opponent’s body before bouncing. What is the correct result?
If a legal shot hits the opponent before bouncing, who wins the point?
What is the ruling when a ball in play strikes a player before the bounce?
A shot hits the opponent’s body in mid-air. What is the official result?
options: The point is replayed as a let
The player who hit the shot wins the point
The player who was struck by the ball wins the point
Play continues after the ball falls to the court
questions.correct_answer: The player who hit the shot wins the point

questions.name: foot_fault
questions.title: Foot fault
questions.question: Which of the following describes a foot fault on serve?
question_stems: Which of the following describes a foot fault on serve?
What constitutes a foot fault when serving?
Which action is a foot fault under the serve rules?
How is a foot fault on serve correctly described?
options: The server swings and misses the ball entirely
The serve lands on the service line
The server’s foot touches the baseline, or the wrong side of the center mark, before contacting the ball
The receiver steps into the court before the serve is struck
questions.correct_answer: The server’s foot touches the baseline, or the wrong side of the center mark, before contacting the ball

questions.name: serve_must_be_struck_before_bouncing
questions.title: Serve must be struck before bouncing
questions.question: May a server allow the tossed ball to bounce on the court and then hit it as a legal serve?
question_stems: May a server allow the tossed ball to bounce on the court and then hit it as a legal serve?
Is a bounce-serve legal if the tossed ball hits the court before contact?
Can the server let the toss bounce and still hit a legal serve?
Does tennis allow the serve to be struck after the tossed ball bounces?
options: Yes, provided the bounce is inside the baseline
Yes, but only on the second serve
Yes, if the receiver agrees before the point
No; the serve must be struck before the ball bounces
questions.correct_answer: No; the serve must be struck before the ball bounces

questions.name: definition_of_a_winner
questions.title: Definition of a winner
questions.question: In standard point classification, which statement correctly defines a winner?
question_stems: In standard point classification, which statement correctly defines a winner?
What correctly defines a winner in tennis point classification?
Which option is the correct definition of a winner?
How is a winner defined, as distinct from a serve ace?
options: A shot, other than the serve, that lands in and is not touched or cannot be returned by the opponent
Any point won by the server
Any error made by the opponent under pressure
A serve that the receiver touches but fails to put back in play
questions.correct_answer: A shot, other than the serve, that lands in and is not touched or cannot be returned by the opponent

questions.name: net_cord_during_a_rally
questions.title: Net cord during a rally
questions.question: During a rally (after a legal serve), a shot clips the net and then lands in the opponent’s court. What is the correct ruling?
question_stems: During a rally (after a legal serve), a shot clips the net and then lands in the opponent’s court. What is the correct ruling?
In a rally, a net-cord shot lands in. What happens?
After the serve, a ball ticks the net and falls in. What is the ruling?
Is a net-cord shot during a rally automatically a let if it lands in?
options: It is always a let and the point is replayed
The ball remains in play; if the opponent cannot return it, the hitter wins the point
The player who hit the shot automatically loses the point
The point is awarded to the receiver of the original serve
questions.correct_answer: The ball remains in play; if the opponent cannot return it, the hitter wins the point

questions.name: shot_into_the_net_during_a_rally
questions.title: Shot into the net during a rally
questions.question: During a rally, a player hits the ball into the net and it does not pass into the opponent’s court. What is the result?
question_stems: During a rally, a player hits the ball into the net and it does not pass into the opponent’s court. What is the result?
What is the result if a rally shot goes into the net and fails to cross?
A player puts the ball into the net during a rally. Who wins the point?
If a shot dies in the net and never reaches the other side, what is the ruling?
options: The point is replayed as a let
The opponent must play the next ball off the net
The player who hit the ball into the net loses the point
The server is awarded a second serve
questions.correct_answer: The player who hit the ball into the net loses the point

questions.name: singles_court_boundaries
questions.title: Singles court boundaries
questions.question: In a singles point, a ball lands outside the singles sideline but inside the doubles sideline (in the alley). How is the ball judged?
question_stems: In a singles point, a ball lands outside the singles sideline but inside the doubles sideline (in the alley). How is the ball judged?
In singles, is a ball landing in the doubles alley in or out?
A singles shot lands in the alley between singles and doubles sidelines. What is the call?
How are the doubles alleys treated for in/out judgments in singles?
options: In, because any lined area of the full court is playable
Let; the point must be replayed
In only if it was a serve
Out, because the doubles alleys are not in play in singles
questions.correct_answer: Out, because the doubles alleys are not in play in singles

questions.name: serve_that_strikes_the_receiver_before_bouncing
questions.title: Serve that strikes the receiver before bouncing
questions.question: A legal serve strikes the receiver’s body before the ball bounces. What is the correct result?
question_stems: A legal serve strikes the receiver’s body before the ball bounces. What is the correct result?
If a good serve hits the receiver before bouncing, who wins the point?
What is the ruling when a legal serve hits the receiver in the air?
A serve is good and strikes the receiver before the bounce. What happens?
options: The server wins the point
The point is replayed as a let
The receiver wins the point
The serve is counted as a fault
questions.correct_answer: The server wins the point

questions.name: point_scoring_sequence_within_a_game
questions.title: Point scoring sequence within a game
questions.question: In standard tennis scoring, what is the correct order of point values within a game (before deuce)?
question_stems: In standard tennis scoring, what is the correct order of point values within a game (before deuce)?
Before deuce, how do point values progress within a game?
What is the standard sequence of points in a tennis game prior to deuce?
Which sequence correctly lists Love, 15, 30, and 40 within a game?
options: 0 (Love), 15, 30, Advantage, Game

questions.name: deuce
questions.title: Deuce
questions.question: If both players have won three points in a game (score 40–40), what is the score called?
question_stems: If both players have won three points in a game (score 40–40), what is the score called?
What is the name of the score when both players are at 40 in a game?
When the game score reaches 40–40, what is that score called?
Both sides have three points in the game. What is the score termed?
options: Advantage server
Game point
Deuce
Match point
questions.correct_answer: Deuce

questions.name: advantage_after_deuce
questions.title: Advantage after deuce
questions.question: From deuce, a player wins the next point. What is the score?
question_stems: From deuce, a player wins the next point. What is the score?
After deuce, what is the score when one player wins the following point?
A player wins the point at deuce. What is the resulting score?
What score follows immediately after a point won from deuce?
options: Game for that player
40–30 for that player
The game returns to 30–30
Advantage for that player
questions.correct_answer: Advantage for that player

questions.name: losing_advantage_back_to_deuce
questions.title: Losing advantage (back to deuce)
questions.question: The score is Advantage to Player A. Player B then wins the next point. What is the score?
question_stems: The score is Advantage to Player A. Player B then wins the next point. What is the score?
From Advantage to Player A, Player B wins the point. What is the new score?
If the player without Advantage wins the next point, what happens to the score?
Advantage Player A is followed by a point for Player B. What is the score now?
options: Deuce
Game for Player B
Advantage Player B
40–30 to Player B
questions.correct_answer: Deuce

questions.name: winning_from_advantage
questions.title: Winning from advantage
questions.question: The score is Advantage to Player A. Player A then wins the next point. What is the result?
question_stems: The score is Advantage to Player A. Player A then wins the next point. What is the result?
From Advantage, the same player wins the next point. What is the result?
Player A holds Advantage and wins the following point. What happens?
What occurs when the player with Advantage wins the next point?
options: The score returns to deuce
Player A wins the game
Player A reaches 40–30
Player A is awarded a set point only
questions.correct_answer: Player A wins the game

questions.name: meaning_of_love
questions.title: Meaning of “Love”
questions.question: In tennis scoring, what does “Love” mean?
question_stems: In tennis scoring, what does “Love” mean?
What does the term Love represent in a tennis score?
In scoring terminology, Love corresponds to which value?
When a score is announced with Love, what does that indicate?
options: Advantage
Deuce
Zero points (or zero games)
Game point
questions.correct_answer: Zero points (or zero games)

questions.name: break_point
questions.title: Break point
questions.question: Which situation correctly defines a break point?
question_stems: Which situation correctly defines a break point?
What is a break point in tennis?
Which statement correctly describes a break point?
When is the receiver said to have a break point?
options: The server can win the game on the next point
Either player can win the set on the next point
The match must be decided by a tiebreak
The receiver can win the server’s service game on the next point
questions.correct_answer: The receiver can win the server’s service game on the next point

questions.name: hold_vs_break
questions.title: Hold vs break
questions.question: What does it mean for a player to “hold serve”?
question_stems: What does it mean for a player to “hold serve”?
Which statement correctly defines holding serve?
What is meant by a service hold?
When has a server successfully held serve?
options: The server wins their own service game
The receiver wins the server’s service game
The server saves a match point
The server hits an ace
questions.correct_answer: The server wins their own service game

questions.name: forced_error_vs_unforced_error
questions.title: Forced error vs unforced error
questions.question: Which statement best distinguishes a forced error from an unforced error?
question_stems: Which statement best distinguishes a forced error from an unforced error?
How do forced and unforced errors differ?
What is the key distinction between a forced error and an unforced error?
Which option correctly contrasts forced error vs unforced error?
options: A forced error always occurs on serve; an unforced error never does
A forced error is caused by opponent pressure; an unforced error is a routine mistake without significant pressure
A forced error ends in a let; an unforced error awards the point immediately
A forced error requires the ball to hit the net; an unforced error requires the ball to land long
questions.correct_answer: A forced error is caused by opponent pressure; an unforced error is a routine mistake without significant pressure

questions.name: one_bounce_only_before_return
questions.title: One bounce only before return
questions.question: After the serve has been put in play, how many times may the ball bounce on a player’s side before that player must return it?
question_stems: After the serve has been put in play, how many times may the ball bounce on a player’s side before that player must return it?
Once the point is in a rally, how many bounces are allowed before a return?
In a rally, what is the maximum number of bounces permitted before playing the ball?
After a legal serve, how many bounces may occur on one side before the ball must be returned?
options: Zero; the ball may never bounce
Two
One
As many as needed if the player stays behind the baseline
questions.correct_answer: One

questions.name: racket_may_strike_the_ball_only_once
questions.title: Racket may strike the ball only once
questions.question: During a point, a player’s racket hits the ball twice in a continuous, intentional double-hit motion. What is the usual ruling under standard rules?
question_stems: During a point, a player’s racket hits the ball twice in a continuous, intentional double-hit motion. What is the usual ruling under standard rules?
What is the ruling for an intentional continuous double hit during a point?
If a player deliberately double-hits the ball in one motion, what happens?
How do standard rules treat an intentional double hit with the racket?
options: The point continues without penalty
The point is replayed as a let
The opponent receives only a warning
The player who made the double hit loses the point
questions.correct_answer: The player who made the double hit loses the point

questions.name: volley_definition_and_legality
questions.title: Volley definition and legality
questions.question: Which statement about a volley is correct?
question_stems: Which statement about a volley is correct?
What correctly describes a volley in tennis?
Which option accurately defines a legal volley?
How is a volley correctly characterized under the rules of play?
options: A volley is a shot struck before the ball bounces and is legal during a rally
A volley is illegal in singles
A volley is allowed only on the second serve
A volley requires the ball to bounce once first
questions.correct_answer: A volley is a shot struck before the ball bounces and is legal during a rally

questions.name: serving_from_the_correct_half
questions.title: Serving from the correct half
questions.question: At the start of a game, from which side of the center mark should the server begin the first point?
question_stems: At the start of a game, from which side of the center mark should the server begin the first point?
Where must the server stand for the first point of a game?
For the opening point of a game, which court half does the server use?
At 0–0 in a game, from which side is the first serve delivered?
options: The ad court (left side from the server’s perspective)
The deuce court (right side from the server’s perspective)
Either side, chosen by the receiver
Either side, alternating randomly each point
questions.correct_answer: The deuce court (right side from the server’s perspective)

questions.name: alternating_serve_sides_within_a_game
questions.title: Alternating serve sides within a game
questions.question: After the first point of a game, where does the server deliver the next serve?
question_stems: After the first point of a game, where does the server deliver the next serve?
Within a game, how do serve sides change from point to point?
Following the first point, from which side is the next serve taken?
Do servers continue from the same side or alternate sides after each point?
options: From the same side as the previous point
From anywhere behind the baseline
From the opposite side of the center mark (alternating sides each point)
From the ad court only for the remainder of the game
questions.correct_answer: From the opposite side of the center mark (alternating sides each point)

questions.name: receiver_hit_by_a_legal_return_before_bouncing
questions.title: Receiver hit by a legal return before bouncing
questions.question: During a rally, Player A hits a legal shot that strikes Player B before bouncing. Who wins the point?
question_stems: During a rally, Player A hits a legal shot that strikes Player B before bouncing. Who wins the point?
If Player A’s legal rally shot hits Player B in the air, who wins?
A ball struck by Player A hits Player B before the bounce. What is the result?
Who is awarded the point when a legal return hits the opponent before bouncing?
options: Player B
Neither; it is a let
The original server of the game, always
Player A
questions.correct_answer: Player A

questions.name: ball_goes_through_the_net
questions.title: Ball goes through the net
questions.question: If a ball passes through a hole in the net into the opponent’s court, what is the correct ruling?
question_stems: If a ball passes through a hole in the net into the opponent’s court, what is the correct ruling?
What is the call when the ball goes through the net rather than over it?
A ball travels through an opening in the net. How is the point decided?
Under the rules, what happens if the ball passes through the net?
options: The point is a let and is replayed
The player who hit the ball wins the point
The opponent wins the point
Play continues as if the ball cleared the net normally
questions.correct_answer: The point is a let and is replayed

questions.name: hindrance_external_disturbance_let
questions.title: Hindrance / external disturbance let
questions.question: A point is interrupted by a sudden external disturbance (for example, a ball rolling onto the court from another court). What is the usual ruling if neither player caused the interruption?
question_stems: A point is interrupted by a sudden external disturbance (for example, a ball rolling onto the court from another court). What is the usual ruling if neither player caused the interruption?
If an outside ball rolls onto the court and interrupts play, what is the usual ruling?
When an external hindrance stops a point and neither player caused it, what happens?
What is the standard call for an unforeseen external disturbance during a point?
options: The player closer to the disturbance loses the point
The point is replayed as a let
The server is awarded the point
The receiver is awarded the point
questions.correct_answer: The point is replayed as a let

questions.name: returning_after_a_legal_bounce
questions.title: Returning after a legal bounce
questions.question: Player A hits a shot that lands in Player B’s court. What may Player B legally do?
question_stems: Player A hits a shot that lands in Player B’s court. What may Player B legally do?
After a shot lands in the opponent’s court, what is a legal response?
A ball bounces once in Player B’s court. What is Player B allowed to do?
When the opponent’s shot lands in, how may the receiving player continue the point?
options: Let the ball bounce twice and still return it
Catch the ball with the hand and claim the point
Return the ball after at most one bounce
Claim a let because the ball landed near the line
questions.correct_answer: Return the ball after at most one bounce

questions.name: service_box_lines_on_serve
questions.title: Service box lines on serve
questions.question: On serve, the ball lands on the center service line of the correct diagonal box. Is the serve good?
question_stems: On serve, the ball lands on the center service line of the correct diagonal box. Is the serve good?
If a serve lands on the center service line of the proper box, is it in?
Does landing on the center service line count as a good serve?
A serve touches the center service line of the correct box. What is the ruling?
options: No; the center service line is out
No; only the service box interior counts
Only if it is a second serve
Yes; the line is part of the service box
questions.correct_answer: Yes; the line is part of the service box

questions.name: game_point_for_the_server
questions.title: Game point for the server
questions.question: The score is 40–30 in favor of the server. What does the next point represent for the server?
question_stems: The score is 40–30 in favor of the server. What does the next point represent for the server?
At 40–30 for the server, what is the next point called for the server?
When the server leads 40–30, what is at stake on the following point?
Server 40–30: what does winning or contesting the next point mean for the server?
options: Game point (the server can win the game by winning the next point)
Break point
Deuce
Set point only if it is also 5–5 in the set
questions.correct_answer: Game point (the server can win the game by winning the next point)

questions.name: meaning_of_a_break
questions.title: Meaning of a break
questions.question: What does it mean when the receiver “breaks” the server?
question_stems: What does it mean when the receiver “breaks” the server?
Which statement correctly defines a service break?
When has the receiver broken the server’s serve?
What is meant by breaking serve?
options: The receiver hits an ace
The receiver wins the server’s service game
The receiver forces a let
The receiver wins a tiebreak point
questions.correct_answer: The receiver wins the server’s service game

questions.name: ball_lands_beyond_the_baseline
questions.title: Ball lands beyond the baseline
questions.question: During a rally, a shot lands clearly beyond the opponent’s baseline. What is the result?
question_stems: During a rally, a shot lands clearly beyond the opponent’s baseline. What is the result?
If a rally shot lands long past the baseline, what is the ruling?
A ball is hit beyond the opponent’s baseline. Who wins the point?
What happens when a shot lands clearly outside beyond the baseline?
options: The point is replayed
The hitter wins the point if the opponent does not reach it
The hitter loses the point (the ball is out)
The ball remains in play until it bounces twice
questions.correct_answer: The hitter loses the point (the ball is out)

questions.name: no_ad_scoring_optional_format
questions.title: No-ad scoring (optional format)
questions.question: Under no-ad scoring, the game reaches deuce. How is the game decided?
question_stems: Under no-ad scoring, the game reaches deuce. How is the game decided?
In no-ad scoring, what happens when the game is at deuce?
How does no-ad scoring resolve a deuce?
At deuce under no-ad rules, how is the game awarded?
options: Players continue until one leads by two points, as in standard scoring
The server automatically wins the game
The game is replayed from 0–0
The next point wins the game (receiver often chooses the side)
questions.correct_answer: The next point wins the game (receiver often chooses the side)
